Logic.title: Logic
Logic.prose:
Logic studies formal languages, proof, models, semantics, consistency, and the foundations of mathematical reasoning.

[Modal logic](modal-logic/README.md) is the largest field, with more than a third of the subject's articles. The
systems K, T, S4 and S5 are
[sound and strongly complete](modal-logic/soundness-and-completeness-of-normal-modal-logic/README.md) for Kripke
models whose accessibility relation is arbitrary, reflexive, reflexive and transitive, or an equivalence relation, and
[filtration](modal-logic/filtration-and-the-finite-model-property/README.md) gives each of them the finite model
property. The field also has the [modal μ-calculus](modal-logic/modal-calculus/README.md), with least and greatest
fixed points, and its [model-checking game](modal-logic/model-checking-game-for-the-modal-calculus/README.md), a parity
game between Verifier and Refuter.

[Propositional logic](propositional-logic/README.md) covers natural deduction and its completeness,
[Craig interpolation](propositional-logic/craig-interpolation/README.md) and satisfiability, from the
[Tseitin transformation](propositional-logic/tseitin-transformation/README.md) and resolution to the DPLL procedure
and binary decision diagrams. [First-order logic](first-order-logic/README.md) centers on
[Gödel's completeness theorem](first-order-logic/g-del-s-completeness-theorem/README.md) in its strong form, built
from Henkin witnesses, and in [temporal logic](temporal-logic/README.md) every formula of linear temporal logic has a
Büchi automaton accepting exactly the words that satisfy it, the basis of
[LTL model checking](temporal-logic/model-checking-for-linear-temporal-logic/README.md).

[Proof theory](proof-theory/README.md) has
[cut elimination for classical linear logic](proof-theory/cut-elimination-for-classical-linear-logic/README.md) and
abstract forms of [Gödel's incompleteness theorems](proof-theory/g-del-s-incompleteness-theorems/README.md), and
[model theory](model-theory/README.md) has Tarski's
[quantifier elimination for the real field](model-theory/quantifier-elimination-for-real-closed-fields/README.md),
Morley's categoricity theorem and [Wilkie's conjecture](model-theory/wilkie-s-conjecture/README.md) for
$\mathbb{R}_{\exp}$, which bounds the number of algebraic points of degree at most $g$ and height at most $H$ on the
transcendental part of a definable set by a polynomial in $g$ and $\log H$.

Algebra.title: Algebra
Algebra.prose:
Algebra studies structures defined by operations and the laws, morphisms, and symmetries that organize them.

Over two fifths of the subject's articles are in [polynomials and power series](polynomials/README.md). Its largest
topic, [deep power-sum congruences](polynomials/deep-power-sum-congruences/README.md), shows that for monic
polynomials over a torsion-free $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$-algebra, congruences of the first $N$ elementary symmetric
functions modulo a divided-power ideal $\mathfrak{a}$ are equivalent to congruences of the $n$-th power sums modulo
$n\mathfrak{a}$ for $n \le N$. [Orthogonal polynomials](orthogonal-polynomials/README.md) include
[Favard's theorem](orthogonal-polynomials/favard-s-theorem/README.md) on three-term recurrences, real
[zeros of polynomials](zeros-of-polynomials/README.md) are counted by Sturm's theorem,
[Lie algebras](nonassociative-algebras/README.md) have
[Ado's theorem](nonassociative-algebras/ado-s-theorem/README.md) and, in characteristic zero, the Levi decomposition,
and [associative algebras](associative-algebras/README.md) include Frobenius's classification of the
finite-dimensional real division algebras and Jacobson's commutativity theorem.

GroupTheory.title: Group Theory
GroupTheory.prose:
Group theory studies symmetry through groups, actions, subgroups, quotients, and structural decompositions.

No single field dominates the subject; the largest,
[characters of finite groups](characters-of-finite-groups/README.md), has about an eighth of its articles. Its largest
topic leads up to [Burnside's $p^a q^b$ theorem](characters-of-finite-groups/burnside-s-p-a-q-b-theorem/README.md),
that a group of order $p^a q^b$ is solvable, and the field also has the
[Frobenius determinant theorem](characters-of-finite-groups/frobenius-group-determinant/README.md) on the
factorization of the group determinant and the
[McKay conjecture](characters-of-finite-groups/mckay-conjecture/README.md), the Cabanes–Späth theorem that a finite
group and the normalizer of a Sylow $p$-subgroup have equally many irreducible characters of degree prime to $p$. The
theory of [finite simple groups](finite-simple-groups/README.md) includes the Gorenstein–Walter theorem on simple
groups with dihedral Sylow $2$-subgroups, and [soluble finite groups](soluble-finite-groups/README.md), the second
largest field, are studied through [formations and Fitting classes](soluble-finite-groups/formations/README.md).

On the infinite side, [geometric group theory](geometric-group-theory/README.md) covers growth, amenability,
hyperbolicity, Thompson's group $F$ and
[property (T)](geometric-group-theory/property-t-for-automorphism-groups-of-free-group/README.md) for
$\operatorname{Aut}(F_n)$ with $n \ge 6$. [Free groups](free-groups/README.md) appear with their subgroups and
automorphisms, and [presentations and decision problems](presentations-and-decision-problems/README.md) include
[braid and Artin groups](presentations-and-decision-problems/braid-and-artin/README.md), a finitely presented group
with unsolvable [word problem](presentations-and-decision-problems/word-problem-for-groups/README.md) (Novikov and
Boone) and finitely presented infinite simple groups. [Permutation groups](permutation-groups/README.md) run from
Frobenius groups to highly homogeneous and cofinitary groups on infinite sets, and in
[group rings](group-rings/README.md) Gardam's unit in $\mathbb{F}_2[P]$, for a torsion-free group $P$, disproves
[Kaplansky's unit conjecture](group-rings/kaplansky-s-unit-conjecture/README.md).

RingTheory.title: Ring Theory
RingTheory.prose:
Ring theory studies addition and multiplication through ideals, modules, localization, dimension, and homological structure.

[Ramification theory](ramification/README.md), the largest field with about a quarter of the subject's articles,
follows primes through finite extensions of Dedekind domains and discrete valuation rings: a prime is unramified
exactly when it does not divide the [discriminant](ramification/different-and-discriminant-ideals/README.md), the norm
of the different, and at an unramified prime with finite residue field the
[Frobenius element](ramification/frobenius-elements/README.md) generates the decomposition group and is trivial
exactly when the prime splits completely. In [Dedekind domains](dedekind-domains/README.md) the
[ideal class group](dedekind-domains/ideal-class-group/README.md) is trivial exactly when the domain is a principal
ideal domain, equivalently a unique factorization domain. [Formal power series](formal-power-series/README.md) include
Hahn series, and the subject also has Hilbert's syzygy theorem, the Quillen–Suslin theorem and the weak
[Nullstellensatz](ideals-and-constructions/hilbert-s-nullstellensatz/README.md) over $\mathbb{C}$.

FieldTheory.title: Field Theory
FieldTheory.prose:
Field theory studies extensions of fields, algebraic elements, automorphisms, and Galois-theoretic structure.

[Galois theory](galois-theory/README.md), with nearly half of the subject's articles, includes the Abel–Ruffini
theorem that every complex root of every rational polynomial of degree $n$ is expressible by
[radicals](galois-theory/solvability-by-radicals/README.md) exactly when $n \le 4$, the
[Gauss–Wantzel theorem](galois-theory/gauss-wantzel-theorem-on-constructible-polygons/README.md) on constructible
regular polygons, and the [essential dimension](galois-theory/essential-dimension-of-symmetric-groups/README.md) of
$S_n$ over $\mathbb{C}$, which lies between $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ and $n - 3$ for $n \ge 5$ (Buhler and Reichstein).
[Finite fields](finite-fields/README.md) appear mostly through polynomials over them, such as the
[permutation polynomials](finite-fields/permutation-polynomials/README.md), where $X^d$ permutes $\mathbb{F}_q$
exactly when $\gcd(d, q - 1) = 1$, and [field extensions and algebraic closure](extensions-and-closure/README.md)
covers [Puiseux's theorem](extensions-and-closure/puiseux-s-theorem/README.md) on the algebraic closure of $K((t))$
for $K$ algebraically closed of characteristic zero.

LinearAlgebra.title: Linear Algebra
LinearAlgebra.prose:
Linear algebra studies vector spaces, linear maps, matrices, duality, dimension, and spectral structure.

The largest field, [special matrices](special-matrices/README.md), a third of the subject, covers circulant matrices,
total positivity, the [Perron–Frobenius theorem](special-matrices/perron-frobenius-theorem/README.md) for irreducible
nonnegative matrices and van der Waerden's lower bound $n!/n^n$ for the permanent of a doubly stochastic $n \times n$
matrix. [Matrix decompositions](matrix-decompositions/README.md) and linear systems include the
[conjugate gradient method](matrix-decompositions/conjugate-gradient-method/README.md), whose energy-norm error after
$k$ steps is at most $2\big((\sqrt{\kappa} - 1)/(\sqrt{\kappa} + 1)\big)^k$ times the initial one, $\kappa$ being the
condition number of the positive definite matrix.
[Eigenvalues and canonical forms](eigenvalues-and-canonical-forms/README.md) include the Jordan normal form of a
matrix whose characteristic polynomial splits, and [positive definite matrices](positive-definite-matrices/README.md)
come with Hadamard's inequality and von Neumann's trace inequality.

NumberTheory.title: Number Theory
NumberTheory.prose:
Number theory studies integers, primes, Diophantine equations, arithmetic functions, and their analytic and algebraic structure.

The subject runs from elementary arithmetic to its analytic and algebraic theories.
[Congruences and power residues](congruences/README.md) build up to
[residue symbols and quadratic reciprocity](congruences/power-residues-reciprocity/README.md). The distribution of
primes, from the [prime number theorem and explicit bounds](distribution-of-primes/prime-number-theorem/README.md), is
approached through the [Riemann zeta function](zeta-l-functions/riemann-zeta/README.md) and
[Dirichlet characters and L-functions](zeta-l-functions/dirichlet-l-functions/README.md), with exponential-sum
estimates such as [Vinogradov's mean value theorem](exponential-sums/vinogradov-s-mean-value-theorem/README.md) as a
tool.

Diophantine questions take several forms: equations such as
[Pell's equation](diophantine-equations/pell-quadratic-equations/README.md), Diophantine approximation through
[Roth's theorem and linear forms in logarithms](diophantine-approximation/roth-linear-forms/README.md), and
representation by sums of powers in [Waring's problem](quadratic-forms-sums-of-squares/waring-figurate/README.md).
[Algebraic number theory](algebraic-number-theory/README.md) and [p-adic numbers](p-adic-numbers/README.md) give the
global and local structure behind them, and [arithmetic geometry](arithmetic-geometry/README.md) reaches elliptic
curves, with [Mazur's torsion theorem](arithmetic-geometry/mazur-s-torsion-theorem/README.md).

The largest field is [linear recurrence sequences](linear-recurrences/README.md): Fibonacci and Lucas numbers, Pell,
Jacobsthal and Tribonacci-type sequences, Lucas sequences and their primitive divisors, and Diophantine problems about
the terms. Arithmetic functions, digits and numeration systems, modular forms and partitions, special numbers such as
the Bernoulli and Catalan numbers, and integer sequences make up much of the rest.

AlgebraicGeometry.title: Algebraic Geometry
AlgebraicGeometry.prose:
Algebraic geometry studies spaces cut out by polynomial equations and translates between their geometric and algebraic invariants.

The largest field, [varieties and projective geometry](varieties-and-projective-geometry/README.md), includes
[Bézout's theorem](varieties-and-projective-geometry/b-zout-s-theorem/README.md) for $n$ hypersurfaces in
$\mathbb{P}^n$ over an algebraically closed field that meet in finitely many points and Seshadri constants of ten
points in the plane, whose generic value Nagata's conjecture predicts to be $1/\sqrt{10}$. For
[elliptic curves](elliptic-curves/README.md) over a field with $q$ elements, the
[Hasse bound](elliptic-curves/hasse-bound/README.md) $(q + 1 - N)^2 \le 4q$ limits the number $N$ of points and
[Waterhouse's theorem](elliptic-curves/point-counts-and-frobenius-traces/README.md) says which integers occur as
$q + 1 - N$. [Algebraic curves](algebraic-curves/README.md) come with the Abel–Jacobi map into the Jacobian and the
uniform bound of Dimitrov, Gao and Habegger on the rational points of curves of genus at least $2$, and
[arithmetic geometry](arithmetic-geometry/README.md) has
[Faltings's theorem](arithmetic-geometry/faltings-s-theorem/README.md) and the Weil conjectures over finite fields.

Geometry.title: Geometry
Geometry.prose:
Geometry studies shapes, spaces, transformations, curvature, and the invariants preserved by geometric equivalence.

[Discrete geometry](discrete-geometry/README.md), the largest field with about a third of the subject's articles,
studies point configurations, lattice points, polyhedra and extremal shapes. Its largest topic,
[continuous Turán numbers](discrete-geometry/part-01/continuous-tur-n-numbers-of-planar-patterns/README.md), concerns
the supremum of the areas of open subsets of $[0, n]^2$ that avoid a planar pattern $P$, which for finite $P$ agrees
up to constant factors with the 0-1 matrix extremal function of $P$. The field also has
[lattice points in dilated regions](discrete-geometry/part-01/lattice-points-in-dilated-regions/README.md), the
[moving sofa](discrete-geometry/part-01/moving-sofa-problem/README.md) constant, between $2.2195$ and $2.37$, the
[Dehn invariant](discrete-geometry/part-01/dehn-invariant/README.md),
[distinct and unit distances](discrete-geometry/part-01/distinct-and-unit-distances/README.md), Monsky's theorem and
the Sylvester–Gallai theorem.

[Packings and coverings](packings-and-coverings/README.md), a fifth of the subject, has the
[Kepler conjecture](packings-and-coverings/kepler-conjecture/README.md) that the supremum of the densities of unit
sphere packings in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is $\pi/\sqrt{18}$, and covering problems such as
[Moser's worm problem](packings-and-coverings/moser-s-worm-problem/README.md),
[Lebesgue's universal covering problem](packings-and-coverings/lebesgue-s-universal-covering-problem/README.md) and
[Hadwiger's covering problem](packings-and-coverings/hadwiger-covering-and-illumination-problem/README.md), with every
convex body in $\mathbb{R}^3$ covered by $14$ translates of its interior. [Convex geometry](convex-geometry/README.md)
includes the
[Brunn–Minkowski and Prékopa–Leindler inequalities](convex-geometry/brunn-minkowski-and-pr-kopa-leindler-inequalitie/README.md)
and [Hadwiger's theorem](convex-geometry/hadwiger-s-theorem-on-valuations/README.md) that the continuous
isometry-invariant valuations on convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^n$ form a space of dimension $n + 1$.

[Euclidean geometry](euclidean-geometry/README.md) runs from
[triangle geometry](euclidean-geometry/triangle-geometry/README.md) to
[isometries and crystallographic groups](euclidean-geometry/isometries-and-symmetry/README.md), with the 17 wallpaper
groups and the 230 space groups. On the smooth side, [Riemannian and Finsler geometry](riemannian-geometry/README.md)
has the [Hopf–Rinow theorem](riemannian-geometry/hopf-rinow-theorem/README.md), the
[sphere theorem](riemannian-geometry/sphere-theorem/README.md) for compact simply connected strictly quarter-pinched
manifolds and [Mostow rigidity](riemannian-geometry/mostow-rigidity-theorem/README.md) for lattices in
$\mathrm{PO}(n, 1)$ with $n \ge 3$, and [curves and surfaces](curves-and-surfaces/README.md) include the
[Fáry–Milnor theorem](curves-and-surfaces/f-ry-milnor-theorem/README.md) that a knot of total curvature at most $4\pi$
is unknotted.

Topology.title: Topology
Topology.prose:
Topology studies continuity, open sets, compactness, connectedness, and invariants preserved by homeomorphism.

[Knot theory](knot-theory/README.md) is the largest field, with nearly half of the subject's articles. It starts from
[knots, links and ambient isotopy](knot-theory/knots-links-and-ambient-isotopy/README.md) and
[knot diagrams](knot-theory/knot-diagrams/README.md), and goes on to geometric questions:
[ropelength and crossing number](knot-theory/ropelength-and-crossing-number/README.md), the
[distortion of knots](knot-theory/distortion-of-knots/README.md) and the
[quadrisecant theorem](knot-theory/quadrisecant-theorem/README.md), with [slice knots](knot-theory/slice-knots/README.md)
on the four-dimensional side.

[General topology](general-topology/README.md) covers dimension theory and the limits and products that build new
spaces, and [descriptive set theory](descriptive-set-theory/README.md) characterizes Baire space, Cantor space and the
rationals and studies the [Banach–Mazur game](descriptive-set-theory/banach-mazur-game/README.md).
[Algebraic topology](algebraic-topology/README.md) includes the
[Hurewicz theorem](algebraic-topology/hurewicz-theorem/README.md) in degree one and the
[homotopy groups of spheres](algebraic-topology/homotopy-groups-of-spheres/README.md), and
[manifolds and geometric topology](manifolds-geometric-topology/README.md) runs from the
[classification of surfaces](manifolds-geometric-topology/classification-of-surfaces/README.md) to the
[Poincaré conjecture](manifolds-geometric-topology/poincar-conjecture/README.md) in dimensions three, four and at least
five and the [annulus theorem](manifolds-geometric-topology/annulus-theorem/README.md) in dimensions at least four. The
[Hilbert cube](continua-infinite-dimensional/hilbert-cube/README.md) and
[absolute retracts](continua-infinite-dimensional/absolute-retracts/README.md) belong to continuum theory and
infinite-dimensional topology.

Analysis.title: Analysis
Analysis.prose:
Analysis studies limits, approximation, continuity, and infinite-dimensional spaces of functions and operators.

[Operator theory](operator-theory/README.md) is the largest field, with a quarter of the subject's articles. Its
largest part, [shift, Toeplitz and Hankel operators](operator-theory/shift-toeplitz-hankel/README.md), starts from the
[unilateral shift](operator-theory/shift-toeplitz-hankel/unilateral-shift/README.md) on $\ell^2(\mathbb{N})$, whose
spectrum is the closed unit disc and whose Fredholm index is $-1$. Concrete operators such as the
[Cesàro operator](operator-theory/integral-and-multiplication/ces-ro-operator/README.md), bounded on $\ell^2$ but not
compact, sit beside general theory: the
[spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators](operator-theory/spectral-theory/spectral-theorem-for-compact-self-adjoint-operat/README.md),
the [homotopy invariance of the Fredholm index](operator-theory/compact-and-fredholm/homotopy-invariance-of-the-fredholm-index/README.md)
and the [Courant–Fischer min–max theorem](operator-theory/eigenvalue-inequalities/courant-fischer-min-max-theorem/README.md).

[Complex analysis](complex-analysis/README.md) runs from [Cauchy theory](complex-analysis/cauchy-theory/README.md) and
the [great Picard theorem](complex-analysis/cauchy-theory/great-picard-theorem/README.md) through the
[Riemann mapping theorem](complex-analysis/geometric-function-theory/riemann-mapping-theorem/README.md) to the Hardy,
Bergman, Dirichlet and Fock [spaces of analytic functions](complex-analysis/analytic-function-spaces/README.md).
[Harmonic analysis](harmonic-analysis/README.md) covers [Fourier series](harmonic-analysis/fourier-series/README.md),
with [Fejér's theorem](harmonic-analysis/fourier-series/fej-r-kernel-and-fej-r-s-theorem/README.md) on the uniform
convergence of the Cesàro means of continuous periodic functions,
[Fourier interpolation](harmonic-analysis/fourier-transform/fourier-interpolation-in-dimensions-8-and-24/README.md) of
radial Schwartz functions in dimensions $8$ and $24$, and
[discrete Fourier analysis](harmonic-analysis/discrete-fourier-analysis/README.md) on finite abelian groups and the
Boolean cube.

[Banach spaces](banach-spaces/README.md) are studied through
[duality and weak topologies](banach-spaces/duality-and-weak-topologies/README.md), from the Hahn–Banach and
Banach–Alaoglu theorems to
[James' reflexivity theorem](banach-spaces/duality-and-weak-topologies/james-reflexivity-theorem/README.md), and
through the [classical sequence spaces](banach-spaces/sequence-spaces/README.md) $\ell^p$ and $c_0$. The rest of the
subject includes [special functions](special-functions/README.md) such as the gamma function and polylogarithms;
[real functions](real-functions/README.md), from nowhere-differentiable functions to the Hyers–Ulam stability of
additive maps; [sequences and series](sequences-and-series/README.md), with Tauberian theorems and series for
constants such as Catalan's constant; and [numerical analysis](numerical-analysis/README.md), from Newton's method to
[Céa's lemma](numerical-analysis/c-a-s-lemma/README.md) for Galerkin approximation.

MeasureTheory.title: Measure Theory
MeasureTheory.prose:
Measure theory provides the language of size and integration underlying probability and modern analysis.

[Geometric measure theory](geometric-measure-theory/README.md), the largest field, is mostly the
[Falconer distance set problem](geometric-measure-theory/falconer-distance-set-problem/README.md) in the plane: the
infimum of the $s$ such that every compact $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ of Hausdorff dimension greater than $s$ has a
distance set of positive Lebesgue measure is at least $1$ and at most $3/2$ (both Falconer), $4/3$ (Wolff) and $5/4$
(Guth, Iosevich, Ou and Wang). By Moran's formula, a
[self-similar set](geometric-measure-theory/hausdorff-dimension-of-self-similar-sets/README.md) generated by $n$
similarities of ratio $\lambda$ under the open set condition has Hausdorff dimension $\log n / \log(1/\lambda)$.
[Measures and measurable sets](measures/README.md) run from Carathéodory's extension theorem to Vitali's nonmeasurable
set and the [Banach–Tarski paradox](measures/banach-tarski-paradox/README.md), and integration, Lebesgue spaces, Haar
measure and optimal transport make up most of the rest.

Probability.title: Probability
Probability.prose:
Probability studies random phenomena through distributions, expectation, independence, concentration, and stochastic processes.

The subject starts from limit theorems for sums of independent variables.
[Laws of large numbers](laws-of-large-numbers/README.md) give almost-sure convergence, with the
[strong law](laws-of-large-numbers/strong-law-of-large-numbers/README.md) and Kolmogorov's three-series theorem, and
[central limit theorems](central-limit-theorems/README.md) give convergence in law, with the
[Berry–Esseen theorem](central-limit-theorems/berry-esseen-theorem/README.md) bounding the error by
$C\rho/(\sigma^3\sqrt{n})$. [Markov chains](markov-chains/README.md) include the convergence theorem for finite
irreducible aperiodic chains, and [stochastic calculus](stochastic-calculus/README.md) has the
[Itô integral](stochastic-calculus/it-integral/README.md) and its isometry.

[Percolation](percolation/README.md) is the largest field, with about an eighth of the articles. For Bernoulli bond
percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with $d \ge 2$ the critical probability lies strictly between $0$ and $1$
([phase transition](percolation/phase-transition/README.md)); below it, the probability that the origin is connected
to distance $n$ decays exponentially in $n$ ([sharpness](percolation/sharpness/README.md)); and on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ at
$p = 1/2$ the [Russo–Seymour–Welsh theorem](percolation/crossings/README.md) keeps the probability of crossing a
rectangle of fixed aspect ratio away from $0$ and $1$. [Correlation inequalities](correlation-inequalities/README.md)
supply the [Harris–FKG and van den Berg–Kesten inequalities](correlation-inequalities/harris-fkg-bk/README.md) and
[Reimer's inequality](correlation-inequalities/reimer-inequality/README.md), and
[high-dimensional probability](high-dimensional-probability/README.md) has bounds on the
[KLS constant](high-dimensional-probability/kannan-lov-sz-simonovits-conjecture/README.md) of log-concave laws.

[Distributions](distributions/README.md), the second largest field, works out the moments, mass functions and tails of
named laws. About a sixth of the subject is statistics: [hypothesis testing](hypothesis-testing/README.md),
[linear models and multivariate analysis](linear-models-multivariate/README.md),
[statistical estimation](statistical-estimation/README.md), [Bayesian statistics](bayesian-statistics/README.md)
around the Dirichlet process, and [nonparametric and survival methods](nonparametric-survival/README.md) such as the
Kaplan–Meier estimator and the Cox proportional hazards model.

Dynamics.title: Dynamical Systems
Dynamics.prose:
Dynamics studies systems evolving through iteration or time, including recurrence, stability, and long-term behavior.

[Ergodic theory](ergodic-theory/README.md) holds just over half of the subject's articles, most of them on the
almost-everywhere convergence of ergodic averages: the
[Birkhoff ergodic theorem](ergodic-theory/birkhoff-ergodic-theorem/README.md) for maps preserving a finite measure,
whose limit is the conditional expectation on the invariant σ-algebra, Kingman's subadditive ergodic theorem, and
Bourgain's theorem along polynomial times. [Topological and symbolic dynamics](topological-symbolic-dynamics/README.md)
has the Curtis–Hedlund–Lyndon theorem, [smooth dynamics](smooth-dynamics/README.md) the
[shadowing lemma](smooth-dynamics/shadowing-lemma/README.md) and the planar entropy formulas of Pesin and Young, and
[low-dimensional dynamics](low-dimensional-dynamics/README.md) the Poincaré–Bendixson theorem. In
[complex dynamics](complex-dynamics/README.md) the [Mandelbrot set](complex-dynamics/mandelbrot-set/README.md) is
connected, and by the [Fatou–Julia dichotomy](complex-dynamics/fatou-julia-dichotomy/README.md) the filled Julia set of
$z^2 + c$ is connected for $c$ in it and a Cantor set otherwise.

node.title: Ergodic theory
node.prose: Ergodic theory studies measure-preserving transformations and their statistical behaviour: ergodic averages, recurrence, mixing and the structure of measure-preserving actions.

node.title: Topological and symbolic dynamics
node.prose: Topological dynamics studies continuous maps of topological spaces through orbits, periodic points and recurrence, and symbolic dynamics studies shift spaces and cellular automata on sequences of symbols.

node.title: Complex dynamics
node.prose: Complex dynamics studies the iteration of holomorphic maps, especially polynomials, together with their Julia sets and parameter spaces such as the Mandelbrot set.

Combinatorics.prose:
Combinatorics studies finite and discrete configurations through counting, extremal structure, and constructive arguments.

[Additive combinatorics](additive-combinatorics/README.md) is the largest field, with about one article in seven. It
runs from [zero-sum problems](additive-combinatorics/zero-sum-subset-sums/README.md) in finite abelian groups and
[sumsets and inverse theorems](additive-combinatorics/sumsets-inverse-theorems/README.md), from the
Cauchy–Davenport–Chowla theorem to the polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa theorem over $\mathbb{F}_2$ of Gowers, Green, Manners

[Combinatorics on words](combinatorics-on-words/README.md), nearly as large, studies
[morphic and Sturmian words](combinatorics-on-words/morphic-sturmian-words/README.md) such as the Fibonacci and

Cobham and Christol, and [finite words](combinatorics-on-words/finite-words/README.md), where Witt's formula counts

[Stirling, Bell and Eulerian numbers](stirling-bell-eulerian/README.md),
[integer partitions](integer-partitions/README.md), [binomial coefficients](binomial-coefficients/README.md) and their
sums, [Catalan numbers and lattice paths](catalan-numbers-lattice-paths/README.md),
[integer compositions](integer-compositions/README.md), [Riordan arrays](riordan-arrays-transforms/README.md),

GraphTheory.title: Graph Theory
GraphTheory.prose:
Graph theory studies vertices and edges through connectivity, coloring, minors, flows, and extremal structure.

[Planar graphs and minors](planar-graphs-and-minors/README.md) is the largest field, with over two fifths of the
subject's articles, most of them on curves and regions in the square lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$. The
[discrete Jordan curve theorem](planar-graphs-and-minors/discrete-jordan-curve-theorem-for-the-square-lat/README.md)
gives a connected lattice subgraph with as many edges as vertices exactly one bounded region,
[Hopf's Umlaufsatz](planar-graphs-and-minors/hopf-s-umlaufsatz-for-lattice-polygons/README.md) says that a simple
closed lattice walk with at least three steps and no U-turns turns through $\pm 4$ quarter turns, and a
[discrete Gauss–Bonnet formula](planar-graphs-and-minors/discrete-gauss-bonnet-formula-for-polyominoes/README.md)
relates the corners of a polyomino to its Euler characteristic. Beyond the lattice, the field has the
[Robertson–Seymour theorem](planar-graphs-and-minors/graph-minors/README.md): every minor-closed family of finite
graphs is defined by finitely many forbidden minors.

[Graph coloring](graph-coloring/README.md) has the theorems of Brooks and Vizing, the
[four color theorem](graph-coloring/part-01/four-color-theorem/README.md), the
[Kneser–Lovász theorem](graph-coloring/part-01/kneser-graphs/README.md) that the Kneser graph $K(n, k)$ has chromatic
number $n - 2k + 2$, and the weak perfect graph theorem.
[Algebraic graph theory](algebraic-graph-theory/README.md) has
[Kirchhoff's matrix-tree theorem](algebraic-graph-theory/part-01/kirchhoff-s-matrix-tree-theorem/README.md), and the
pentagon has [Shannon capacity](graph-invariants-and-labelings/shannon-capacity-of-a-graph/README.md) $\sqrt{5}$.
[Matchings and flows](matchings-and-flows/README.md) has the existence of stable matchings in the
[stable marriage problem](matchings-and-flows/stable-marriage-problem/README.md), Kőnig's theorem and the
[max-flow min-cut theorem](matchings-and-flows/max-flow-min-cut-theorem/README.md), and
[paths, cycles and connectivity](paths-cycles-connectivity/README.md) has
[Menger's theorem](paths-cycles-connectivity/menger-s-theorem/README.md), the theorems of Dirac and Ore on Hamiltonian
cycles, and [Fleischner's theorem](paths-cycles-connectivity/fleischner-s-theorem/README.md) that the square of a
2-connected graph is Hamiltonian.

TheoryOfComputation.title: Theory of Computation
TheoryOfComputation.prose:
The mathematical study of what can be computed and at what cost: machine models, computability and undecidability, automata and formal languages, and computational complexity.

[NP-completeness](np-completeness/README.md) is the largest field, with over two fifths of the subject's articles. It
starts from the [Cook–Levin theorem](np-completeness/cook-levin/README.md), that SAT is in NP and every problem in NP
reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction, and establishes NP-completeness problem by problem, from
variants of [satisfiability](np-completeness/satisfiability/README.md) to Hamiltonian cycles, clique, graph coloring
and subset sum. [Complexity classes](complexity-classes/README.md) has Savitch's theorem, the Immerman–Szelepcsényi
theorem $\mathrm{NL} = \mathrm{coNL}$ and Ladner's theorem, and
[hierarchy theorems and barriers](hierarchy-theorems-and-barriers/README.md) has the time hierarchy theorem and the
Baker–Gill–Solovay [oracles](hierarchy-theorems-and-barriers/relativization-and-oracle-separations/README.md) relative
to which P and NP differ or coincide.

In [regular languages](regular-languages/README.md), Kleene's theorem identifies the languages of finite automata with
those of regular expressions, and [minimization](regular-languages/minimization/README.md) rests on the Myhill–Nerode
theorem. [Context-free languages](context-free-languages/README.md) has normal forms, CYK and Earley recognizers, the
equivalence of grammars with [pushdown automata](context-free-languages/grammars-and-pushdown-automata/README.md), and
the pumping and Ogden lemmas, and [decision procedures](decision-procedures/README.md) decide emptiness and
equivalence of finite automata and emptiness of context-free grammars.

[Turing machines](turing-machines/README.md), from single-tape and multi-tape machines to universal ones, compute
exactly the recursive functions ([equivalence of models](equivalence-of-models/README.md)).
[Computability](computability/README.md) has Rice's theorem and the
[undecidability of the halting problem](computability/halting-problem-and-rice-s-theorem/README.md), Kleene's
[recursion theorem](computability/kleene-s-recursion-theorem/README.md) and the
[Busy Beaver](computability/busy-beaver/README.md) value $\Sigma(5) = 4098$, and
[undecidable problems](undecidable-problems/README.md) include the
[Post correspondence problem](undecidable-problems/post-correspondence-problem/README.md) and
[Hilbert's tenth problem](undecidable-problems/diophantine-sets-and-hilbert-s-tenth-problem/README.md), by the theorem
of Davis, Putnam, Robinson and Matiyasevich that the recursively enumerable sets are the Diophantine ones.

ComputerScience.title: Computer Science
ComputerScience.prose:
Computer science formalizes algorithms, programming-language structures, data abstractions, and correctness properties.

[Data structures](data-structures/README.md) is the largest field, with over a quarter of the articles. It develops
each structure with its invariants and the cost of its operations:
[search trees](data-structures/search-trees/README.md) from binary search trees to AVL, red–black and B-trees,
[heaps](data-structures/heaps/README.md), hash tables, tries and union-find.
[Graph algorithms](graph-algorithms/README.md) come with their correctness and cost, from
[shortest paths](graph-algorithms/shortest-paths/README.md) by Dijkstra's algorithm, Bellman–Ford and Floyd–Warshall
to [spanning trees, flows and matchings](graph-algorithms/spanning-trees-flows-matchings/README.md) by the algorithms
of Kruskal, Prim, Edmonds–Karp and Gale–Shapley.

[Process calculi](process-calculi/README.md), the second largest field, is mostly
[session types](process-calculi/session-types/README.md) for the π-calculus, with subject reduction and progress for
typed processes. [Type systems and lambda calculi](type-systems-and-lambda-calculi/README.md) has
[Hindley–Milner type inference](type-systems-and-lambda-calculi/hindley-milner-type-inference/README.md), where
Algorithm W is sound and complete and finds principal types, relational parametricity for
[System F](type-systems-and-lambda-calculi/system-f/README.md) and
[System Fω](type-systems-and-lambda-calculi/system-f-2/README.md), and strong normalization of the
[calculus of constructions](type-systems-and-lambda-calculi/calculus-of-constructions/README.md).
[Programming-language semantics](programming-language-semantics/README.md) gives the IMP language operational and
denotational semantics and a correct compiler to a stack machine.

[Machine learning](machine-learning/README.md) covers
[probabilistic graphical models](machine-learning/probabilistic-graphical-models/README.md) such as Bayesian networks
and hidden Markov models, Bayesian inference, supervised learning, and
[online learning and boosting](machine-learning/online-learning-and-boosting/README.md), with Novikoff's perceptron
mistake bound and the Freund–Schapire bound on the training error of AdaBoost.

InformationTheory.title: Information Theory
InformationTheory.prose:
Information theory quantifies information, uncertainty, compression, and transmission through entropy and coding.

The two largest fields, with nearly two thirds of the articles between them, are
[source coding](source-coding/README.md) and [error-correcting codes](error-correcting-codes/README.md). Source coding
is mostly [Huffman coding](source-coding/huffman-coding/README.md) and its optimality, with
[Shannon's source coding theorem](source-coding/shannon-s-source-coding-theorem/README.md), which puts the least
expected length of a uniquely decodable code over $q \ge 2$ letters between the base-$q$ entropy and one letter more.
Error-correcting codes run from [linear codes](error-correcting-codes/linear-codes/README.md) and the perfect Hamming
$(7,4)$ code to [Reed–Solomon codes](error-correcting-codes/reed-solomon-codes/README.md), which meet the Singleton
bound, and good locally testable codes. [Entropy and mutual information](entropy-and-mutual-information/README.md) and
[information inequalities](information-inequalities/README.md) such as Fano's set up the basic quantities, and
[channel simulation](channel-simulation/README.md) asks how small $H(Y \mid S)$ can be for an auxiliary variable $S$,
independent of the input $X$, that determines the output $Y$ together with $X$.

GameTheory.title: Game Theory
GameTheory.prose:
Game theory studies strategic and combinatorial interaction, equilibria, winning conditions, and optimal play.

Almost all of the subject is [combinatorial games](combinatorial-games/README.md), most of them impartial. The
[Sprague–Grundy theorem](combinatorial-games/sprague-grundy-theorem/README.md) makes every impartial game equivalent to
a Nim heap, and the field works out P-positions and Grundy values game by game, from
[Wythoff's game](combinatorial-games/wythoff-s-game/README.md), whose P-positions are the pairs
$(\lfloor n\varphi \rfloor, \lfloor n\varphi \rfloor + n)$ and their reflections, to variants of Nim, chocolate bar
games and [Sylver Coinage](combinatorial-games/sylver-coinage/README.md), where opening with a prime greater than $3$
wins. The partizan game [Snort](combinatorial-games/snort/README.md) is a second-player win on opposable graphs.
[Social choice](social-choice/README.md) has the theorems of Arrow and of Gibbard and Satterthwaite, and
[cooperative games](cooperative-games/README.md) the
[Bondareva–Shapley theorem](cooperative-games/bondareva-shapley-theorem/README.md): a game with transferable utility
has a nonempty core exactly when it is balanced.

Biology.title: Mathematical Biology
Biology.prose:
Mathematical biology models populations, genomes, and biochemical networks, from coalescents and reaction dynamics to the algorithms that read biological sequences.

[Population genetics](population-genetics/README.md) follows allele frequencies under drift, selection and mutation.
Over half of it is the [diffusion theory](population-genetics/diffusion-theory/README.md) of the Wright–Fisher
diffusion, from Kimura's fixation probability $(1 - e^{-2\sigma x})/(1 - e^{-2\sigma})$ for an allele at frequency
$x$ with scaled selection coefficient $\sigma = 2Ns$ to Wright's beta stationary law under two-way mutation, and the
[Ewens sampling formula](population-genetics/ewens-sampling-formula-and-the-chinese-restauran/README.md) gives the law
of the allelic partition of a sample under the neutral infinite-alleles model.
[Coalescent theory](coalescent-theory/README.md) traces genealogies backward in time: under
[Kingman's coalescent](coalescent-theory/kingman-s-coalescent-and-watterson-s-estimator/README.md) Watterson's
estimator of $\theta$ is unbiased, and the
[multispecies coalescent](coalescent-theory/multispecies-coalescent/README.md) has an anomaly zone, where a gene tree
that disagrees with the species tree is more probable than the one that agrees.

[Bioinformatics](bioinformatics/README.md) is the largest field, with about a sixth of the articles, and over half of
it is [sequence alignment](bioinformatics/sequence-alignment/README.md), from Needleman–Wunsch and Smith–Waterman to
affine-gap, linear-space and wavefront alignment and profile hidden Markov models.
[Phylogenetics](phylogenetics/README.md) reconstructs trees from sequences, with the
[Jukes–Cantor model](phylogenetics/jukes-cantor-model/README.md), neighbor joining and
[Felsenstein's pruning algorithm](phylogenetics/felsenstein-s-pruning-algorithm/README.md).
[Statistical genetics](statistical-genetics/README.md) treats genome-wide association studies, with
[LD score regression](statistical-genetics/ld-score-regression/README.md) and Mendelian randomization;
[population structure](population-structure/README.md) uses Patterson's f-statistics and admixture graphs;
[quantitative genetics](quantitative-genetics/README.md) has Fisher's decomposition of genetic variance; and in
[systems biology](systems-biology/README.md) the
[deficiency-zero theorem](systems-biology/complex-balancing-and-the-deficiency-zero-theore/README.md) gives a weakly
reversible mass-action network of deficiency zero exactly one equilibrium in each positive stoichiometric
compatibility class.

StatisticalMechanics.title: Statistical Mechanics
StatisticalMechanics.prose:
Statistical mechanics studies lattice models of interacting spins and bonds through Gibbs measures, partition functions, correlation inequalities, and phase transitions.

Most of the subject follows the Ising model from a finite graph to the infinite lattice. On a finite graph the
[Lee–Yang circle theorem](spin-models/lee-yang-circle-theorem/README.md) puts the zeros of the ferromagnetic partition
function, as a polynomial in the fugacity $e^{-2\beta h}$ of the external field $h$, on the unit circle, and the
[Griffiths](correlation-inequalities/griffiths-inequalities/README.md) and
[Griffiths–Hurst–Sherman](correlation-inequalities/griffiths-hurst-sherman-inequality/README.md) inequalities control
how spins correlate. On the lattice, the
[Peierls argument](gibbs-states-and-phase-transitions/peierls-argument-for-the-ising-model/README.md) gives long-range
order at low temperature, the ordered half of the
[phase transition](gibbs-states-and-phase-transitions/phase-transition-of-the-ising-model/README.md).

The two-dimensional model is exactly solvable.
[Kramers–Wannier duality](exact-solutions/kramers-wannier-duality/README.md) exchanges high and low temperature.
[Kac–Ward matrices](exact-solutions/kac-ward-matrices/README.md) and
[Sherman's loop cancellations](exact-solutions/sherman-s-loop-cancellations-and-product-formula/README.md) relate
Kac–Ward determinants to sums over closed walks, the
[spin Kac–Ward identities](exact-solutions/spin-kac-ward-identities/README.md) express the partition function on the
torus through four such determinants, and
[Onsager's solution](exact-solutions/onsager-s-solution-of-the-two-dimensional-ising/README.md) computes the free energy
per site in the infinite-volume limit.

The largest field is the [random-cluster model](random-cluster-model/README.md). The
[Edwards–Sokal coupling](random-cluster-model/edwards-sokal-coupling-and-the-fk-representation/README.md) couples Potts
and Ising spins with random subgraphs, turning spin correlations into connection probabilities, and from measures on
finite graphs the field builds infinite-volume measures, the free energy and the critical point.
[Random currents and the switching lemma](random-currents-and-sharpness/random-currents-and-the-switching-lemma/README.md)
lead to the [sharpness of the phase transition](random-currents-and-sharpness/sharpness-of-the-phase-transition-for-the-ising/README.md)
for the Ising model.
